27.0.0.en: “In that day the LORD with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.” [1].

27.0.1.en: Some see in the expression “in that day” a reference to the last day, in which God strikes Satan his final, decisive blow, when the Church enjoys eternal life and the enemy of good perishes, and the followers of the millennial reign try to count it as the day of the thousand-year reign, when the dominion of the devil is shattered; but we see it as the day of the cross, or the day of redemption, in which the Lord reigned from the tree of the cross, and in which He “blotted out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us... and having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it” (Col 2:14-15), for the (spiritual) thousand-year reign began with the crucifixion of the Lord.

27.0.2.en: As I said before, the tendency of some commentators to apply Isaiah's prophecies of the Messianic age to the thousand-year reign is the natural fruit of present-day Christians not tasting the power of the cross in their lives, not experiencing the divine authority against the devil and his works, and not being in touch with the inner life of victory, full of joy and a peace that surpasses understanding.

27.0.3.en: What is this sore sword with which the Lord punishes Leviathan but the word of God, the sharp two-edged sword that goes out of His mouth (Rev 1:16; Heb 4:12)? Through the word we meet Christ Himself, “the incarnate, crucified Word of God,” hidden behind the letters and words, always working for our salvation. As Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says: [The Son of God is living and active, working day by day for the salvation of all.]

27.0.4.en: The punishing of the serpent with the sword and the slaying of the dragon of the sea mean that the incarnate Word of God, our crucified Christ who dwells within us, takes over the leadership of the battle to judge every evil in us until He shatters all darkness, establishing in us the kingdom of light.

27.0.5.en: * He has overcome the whole world, as we see, beloved... He conquered not by military power but by the foolishness of the cross... His body was lifted up on the cross, and the spirits submitted to Him.

27.0.6.en: St. Augustine * The Lord despoiled the principalities and powers and triumphed over them by His cross. And this was the reason for our Lord's coming: to cast them out and to recover man, who is His house and His temple.

27.0.7.en: St. Macarius the Great In our study of “The Holy Spirit between the New Birth and Continual Renewal” we saw that the rite of Baptism, which in truth is an enjoyment of dying with the Lord Christ, being buried with Him, and enjoying the power of His resurrection, rests on two main lines: the enjoyment of the new man, who is in the image of his Creator, and the shattering of the works of the old man; that is, the enjoyment of the Lord Christ and the renouncing of the devil and all his powers and works. In the waters of Baptism we are united with our Christ the King, crucified, who shatters Leviathan the deceiving serpent and the dragon that dwells in the waters.

27.0.8.en: * After you have bent your knees, you are asked to utter these words: “I renounce you, Satan”... What has happened? What is this sudden, strange change? You who trembled with fear, do you rebel against your master? Do you look at his counsel with contempt? What has brought you to this madness? When did this boldness come upon you? You say: We have a sword; a strong sword.

27.0.9.en: What sword is this? What ally do you have? Tell me.

27.0.10.en: You answer: We are entering Your service, O Christ, and therefore we are bold and rebellious, because we have a strong refuge. This has set us above Satan. We who before were terrified of him and feared him, not only renounce him alone, but with him all his pomps.

27.0.11.en: * The priests ask you to say: I renounce you, Satan, and all your pomps and all your service and all your works.

27.0.12.en: Few words, but of great power!

27.0.13.en: The angels stand beside you, and the invisible powers rejoice at your change, and they receive the words from your tongues and carry them to the Master of all creation, to be inscribed there in the books of heaven.

27.1.0.en: 2 In that day sing ye unto the desirable vineyard. 3 I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day. 4 Fury is not in me: who would set the briers and thorns against me in battle? I would go through them, I would burn them together. 5 Or let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me. 6 He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit. 7 Hath he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him? or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him? 8 In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind. 9 By this therefore shall the iniquity of Jacob be purged; and this is all the fruit to take away his sin; when he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the groves and images shall not stand up.

27.2.0.en: Since the Lord Himself takes over the leadership of the battle, He becomes personally a party to it, so that the desirable vineyard may enjoy His victory, His keeping of her, and His care and concern for her. Therefore the prophet says on the tongue of the Lord: “In that day sing ye unto the desirable vineyard. I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day...” [3-5].

27.2.1.en: God Himself is the owner of the vineyard; He loves her and desires her, and He is the vinedresser and keeper of her; He tends her every moment, watering her with His divine blessings; His eye is upon her night and day; He does not leave her or forsake her; He removes the thorns and briers from her to burn them, and reconciles her with the Father through His cross (Rom 5:1).

27.2.2.en: If the cross shattered the devil and stripped him of his authority over the believers, it also offered the following blessings:

27.2.3.en: A. “Sing ye unto the desirable vineyard” [3]. To whom is this said, if not to the heavenly beings who perceived the fruits of the cross in the life of the Church, so that their life exulted and they began to praise God the Savior of mankind for His wondrous work in them, for He made the earthly heavenly, and raised the Church up to the throne to share with heaven its praises and its liturgies. The vineyard desired by God her Savior has become the object of desire of the angels and all the heavenly orders (Rev 5:11-14).

27.2.4.en: If the remembrance of God is the desire of man's soul, that is a response to God's love for us and His desire for us, since we are His desirable vineyard and His beloved bride and His Church in which He desires to dwell. The psalmist says: “For the LORD hath chosen Zion; he hath desired it for his habitation. This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it” (Ps 132:13-14); “This is the hill which God desireth to dwell in; yea, the LORD will dwell in it for ever” (Ps 68:16).

27.2.5.en: B. Divine keeping: “I the LORD do keep it... I will keep it night and day” [3]. If God sends His angels to protect His people from temporal dangers, He Himself undertakes to keep her from the deadly blows of sin. The enemy was shattered by the cross, not as a historical event of the past but as a divine work that is present and active; He fixed His cross in the midst of His Church to embrace her from every blow of the enemy so long as she remains in His embrace and asks for His keeping. Therefore St. Ephrem the Syrian says: [Glory to You who set up Your cross as a bridge over death, on which souls cross from the dwelling of death to the dwelling of life.]

27.2.6.en: C. Continual care: “I will water it every moment” [3]; for He sends down upon her the rains of His free grace, and turns her wilderness into a divine paradise. Therefore she converses with Him, saying: “Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits” (Song 4:16). What I bear of the fruits of the Spirit is His work in me, the fruit of His unceasing care.

27.2.7.en: With what does God water His Church, the desirable vineyard?

27.2.8.en: He gives us His Holy Spirit working in us, gives us His life in us... He gives us Himself!

27.2.9.en: * Generous is He who gives us the greatest of all gifts, His very life!

27.2.10.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * Because of the grace of the Spirit that was given to us, we are in Him and He is in us (1 Jn 4:13)...

27.2.11.en: Apart from the Spirit we are strangers to God and far from Him, but by communion in the Spirit we have become near to the divinity; our being in the Father is not of ourselves but is the work of the Spirit who dwells within us.

27.3.0.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic D. Her not being condemned: “Fury is not in me” [4]. When she receives His free gift and responds practically to His grace, she does not fall under the divine wrath but says with confidence: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus hath made me free from the law of sin and death” (Rom 8:1-2).

27.3.1.en: Some hold that the word “fury” should be read here “hemah,” which means “grapes”; for when He did not find good grapes but thorns and briers, or wild grapes, He burned the thorns and briers to give opportunity for good fruit-bearing.

27.3.2.en: E. The burning of the thorns and briers: “Would that I had the thorns and briers in battle, that I might go against them and burn them together” [4]. He took upon Himself the resisting of the thorns and briers that choke the desirable vineyard, saying: “Would that I had the thorns...” Indeed He bore the thorns on His head when He was crucified, removing the shame, or the curse, from us to bear it for us. As St. Jacob of Serugh says: [He bore the curse of the earth by the crown they placed on His head, and bore the weight of the whole world like a mighty one...! He became a curse that the returning heirs might be blessed through Him! By His crown He uprooted the cursed seed of the serpent... By the crown of thorns He demolished the crown of Satan, who wanted to be god over creation! From His crown of thorns He wove a crown for the daughter of the Gentiles, the bride whom He betrothed from among the idols and wrote down for His name.]

27.4.0.en: F. Our reconciliation with God: “Or let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me” [5]. This is the end of the work of the cross: our reconciliation with God, for when we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of His Son (Rom 5:10).

27.4.1.en: * The Son of God suffered to make us sons of God, and the son of man (we humans) refuses to suffer so that his sonship to God may continue!!!

27.5.0.en: St. Cyprian G. The growth of the universal Church or the new Israel: “In the future Jacob shall take root; Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with fruit” [6]. Perhaps God wanted them not to look to His work with them in the near future (their salvation from the Babylonian captivity) but to the distant future, where the new Jacob takes root, and the Church of the New Covenant arises as the new Israel, which included from among the Jews the disciples and Apostles and many believers who brought forth surpassing spiritual fruits that filled the face of the world. St. Irenaeus says: [The seed was cast into all the world... for from this (Jerusalem) Christ and the Apostles were able to bring forth fruits.]

27.6.0.en: H. His discipline of His children [7-9]: He treats them as sons and not as enemies, so He allows them to be disciplined for their salvation and edification, saying: “Hath he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him?” [7], meaning: has God smitten Jacob Israel as He smote those who smote Jacob? When He strikes His people it is for their edification, but as for the blow to the enemies who smite His people, let it demolish them, because they persist in denial and resistance to God. In the same sense He says: “Or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him?” [7].

27.7.0.en: “With a rebuke (by measure), when thou didst put her away, thou didst contend with her; he removed her with his rough wind in the day of the east wind” [8]. Even in contending, He contends with her as by measure, that is, He allows her affliction as much as she can bear, to discipline her for her sins, even if it seems that He has divorced her and delivered her to the tempestuous wind coming from the east, that is, to Assyria or Babylon in 722 B.C. and 587 B.C.

27.8.0.en: 10 Yet the defenced city shall be desolate, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof. 11 When the boughs thereof are withered, they shall be broken off: the women come, and set them on fire: for it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them, and he that formed them will shew them no favour.

27.8.1.en: In contrast to His discipline of His children, even if it seemed harsh, using Assyria and Babylon, or as one who had divorced them, He permits the destruction of the evil enemy; He turns Babylon, the fortified city, into a forsaken habitation, left like a wilderness.

27.8.2.en: Some hold that the talk here is also about Samaria, which became a ruin because of its people's spiritual ignorance and their withdrawal from the worship of God and falling into idolatry [19-11].

27.9.0.en: 12 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel. 13 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem.

27.9.1.en: Some see in this a prophecy of the gathering of the people of Israel at the end of the ages when they accept faith in the Lord Christ, while others see it as a picture of God's work through the ages when He brought His people out of Egypt and then saved them from the Babylonian captivity.

27.9.2.en: Perhaps it points here to the new Israel, the Church gathered from among the peoples and nations to enjoy the risen life.

28.0.0.en: 1 Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine! 2 Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one, which as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm, as a flood of mighty waters overflowing, shall cast down to the earth with the hand. 3 The crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, shall be trodden under feet: 4 And the glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley, shall be a fading flower, and as the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up. 5 In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people, 6 And for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate.

28.0.1.en: God brings woe upon Samaria, or Ephraim, permitting Assyria in 722 B.C. to overrun the land, ruin the cities and carry away great numbers into captivity. This was a discipline for Israel and a practical lesson for Judah; the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the capital of Judah, were able to go up on the roofs and see the sky reddened with God's wrath against Israel, for tongues of fire rose from many houses of Samaria and its surroundings. Yet the kingdom of Judah did not take warning, for afterward it walked in the same sins of Samaria and even more, as in the parable of Aholah and Aholibah in Ezekiel 33, which tells this matter in some detail.

28.0.2.en: Verses [1-6] depict the fall of Samaria, which was built on a high hill with delightful gardens surrounding it on every side, so that it was counted among the most beautiful and beloved cities of Palestine. The valley beneath it reaches to the coast of Jezreel, rich in vineyards and fruitful fields. God had given them an abundance of good things and wealth, but they left the Giver of the gifts and turned aside to the pagan gods worshiped by the surrounding nations; and their worship was bound up with a pampered, luxurious life together with many abominations; therefore God wanted to discipline them. He stirred the heart of the king of Assyria to look upon beautiful, rich Samaria and the cities around it, so he sent a great army to occupy it. But Israel relied on her human arm and forgot her God, and supposed that she was able to shatter the enemy; so her capital and many of her cities were shattered and became a living example for everyone who relies on the human arm, ignoring God's providence.

28.0.3.en: The prophet presents a wonderful poetic picture of the destruction of Samaria and the glory of the faithful remnant:

28.0.4.en: A. The rich of Samaria were accustomed to hold constant banquets in which they served wine and strong drink without measure, so they got drunk and made merry, and they used to put wreaths of flowers on their heads as a sign of glory and for adornment.

28.1.0.en: The prophet sees the city of Samaria, the head of the cities of Israel, surrounded by gardens, like the head of one of these rich men who eats and drinks and makes merry and gets drunk and practices abominations with a wreath of flowers on his head. God brings woe upon these wreaths, so that they become a shame and a disgrace rather than glory and splendor; their appearance fades, and they deserve to go down with the head that bears them to the dust, to be thrown on the dunghill and trodden underfoot [2-3].

28.1.1.en: B. The Lord sends the army of Assyria as one mighty (strong) and powerful man [2]... It is as though what was accomplished at the hands of the army of the king of Assyria was neither coincidence nor human planning or human resources, but by divine permission that gives them ability and strength and gives them unity to carry out a divine plan, namely the discipline of Samaria!

28.1.2.en: C. The army of Assyria, which besieges Samaria and humbles her, is likened to one who brings down to the dust the head of a rich man bearing a wreath of flowers, with a snowstorm and sweeping floods of water. The rose cannot bear the snow and so it dies, and it cannot bear the floods of water, so it is swept violently to the ground without settling until it becomes an inseparable part of the dunghill [2].

28.2.0.en: D. He likens Samaria to a fig tree bearing a few first fruits that are plucked in moments, and no fruit remains on it [4].

28.3.0.en: E. If God allows this humiliation, removing all glory and splendor for the sake of discipline, He Himself comes forward to be glory and splendor to His believers: “In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people, and for a spirit of judgment to him that sitteth in judgment, and for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate” [5-6]. God becomes our beauty, and the diadem of our splendor, and also our justice, the defender of the poor and the wronged, and the leader of our battle, giving us spiritual victory against the powers of darkness.

28.3.1.en: In contrast to the collapse that befell Samaria, which represents the denial of the faith, God offers Himself as splendor of glory, righteousness, justice and victory to the remnant of His people who are faithful to Him [5]; and the following is to be noted here:

28.3.2.en: First: He says: “In that day” [5]; it is the day of redemption or crucifixion on which the Lord bore our shame on the cross that He Himself might become our crown. He accepted death for us to give us His life and His resurrection and His righteousness; He bore weakness to give us, by His weakness, the power of victory.

28.3.3.en: St. John Chrysostom speaks of the cross as a sign of glory and power... saying:

28.3.4.en: [The cross is glory. Look at what the Evangelist says... “for the Holy Ghost was not yet given; because that Jesus was not yet glorified” (Jn 7:39).

28.3.5.en: The cross is that which removed the enmity between God and men, bringing reconciliation, making the earth heaven, joining angels with men, shattering the fortress of death, weakening the might of Satan, quenching the dominion of sin, rescuing the world from error and recovering the truth, driving out demons, demolishing the temples of idols and transforming their altars and abolishing their sacrifices, sowing virtue and founding the Church!

28.3.6.en: The cross is the will of the Father, the glory of the Son, and the joy of the Holy Spirit. It is the subject of Paul's boasting when he says: “But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Gal 6:14).

28.3.7.en: The cross is brighter than the sun, and more radiant than its rays, for when the sun was darkened the cross shone forth. The sun was darkened not because it was extinguished but because the brightness of the cross overcame it...

28.3.8.en: The cross breaks our chains and abolishes the prison of death.

28.3.9.en: It is the sign of God's love (Jn 3:16)...

28.3.10.en: The cross is a strong fortress and an impregnable shield, protector of the rich, and a spring for the poor, defender of those fallen into the snares, and armor for those on the attack, and a means of conquering the passions and obtaining the virtues, and a wondrous, astonishing sign!].

28.3.11.en: Second: Who is the remnant of His chosen people that adorns itself with the LORD of hosts, is justified by Him and overcomes? Some hold that the talk here is of the kingdom of Judah, which for a time remained in a better state than Ephraim; others see that this remnant are those who accepted faith in the crucified Lord Christ, such as the Apostles and disciples and the Marys and Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, and so on... and others see that it is the remnant that will be saved in the days of the Antichrist, when the spirit of apostasy prevails in the world, but for the sake of the elect God shortens the days (Mt 24:22)...

28.3.12.en: In any case, this remnant includes every soul that runs to the Savior, the LORD of hosts, to hide in Him and rest at His feet and take shelter under His cross, whatever the time may be!

28.4.0.en: 7 But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment. 8 For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean. 9 Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts. 10 For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little: 11 For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. 12 To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear. 13 But the word of the LORD was unto them precept upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little; that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken. 14 Wherefore hear the word of the LORD, ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem. 15 Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:

28.4.1.en: After speaking of the discipline of Ephraim, it seems that he returned to speak of the sins of Judah, for he says: “But they also” [7]; he exposed and denounced them, depicting the extent of Judah's moral dissolution:

28.4.2.en: A. Drunkenness: “They also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink” [7]. If the leaders in Samaria, the capital of Israel, had been corrupted by strong drink, the religious leaders in Jerusalem gave in to the same error.

28.4.3.en: By the prophet here he means the “false prophets” who prophesied out of their own heads to flatter the dissolute priests and the civil leaders. These, as is stated in the Book of Jeremiah, used to speak smooth things, that is, soft, deceptive words, saying that the people were well and at peace and that no disciplines would come upon Jerusalem or the temple... and this is the natural fruit of abandoning the word of God and being entangled in material and moral gain.

28.4.4.en: If this is the state of the priest and the prophet, what then is the state of the people?!

28.4.5.en: B. Error and injustice: “They err in vision, they stumble in judgment” [7]. Since the priest and the false prophet reeled with strong drink, they lost their spiritual awareness and offered misleading visions, because their inner sight had been darkened. And for the same reason they lost the ability to judge justly, so they caused unrest and confusion among the people.

28.4.6.en: In other words, every sin hands man over to another sin; the preoccupation of the priest and the prophet with tables and a life of luxury drew them into absorption in drinking wine until they fell into drunkenness, and this corrupts their inner sight, so they offer misleading visions, and consequently they lose their ability to be just and judge unjustly...

28.5.0.en: C. False prophecies: “For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean” [8].

28.5.1.en: The prophet sees the tables filling the city, and everyone absorbed in eating and drinking greedily without limit, until they vomited in order to return and eat, and this was the custom of the Romans. The whole place, indeed the whole city, became full of vomit and filth, so that no place could be found where a man could rest.

28.5.2.en: This outward picture reveals the spiritual state of Judah, for the false prophets vomited prophecies of their own making and filled the place with what is neither clean nor holy.

28.5.3.en: This is the picture of the reckless man whose whole being is corrupted by the passions, so that his soul, and likewise his heart, his mind, his feelings and all his energies and talents, are filled with abominations, until he becomes like a city full of corruption; so the holy Savior says: “but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head” (Mt 8:20).

28.5.4.en: Man corrupted life, so the Holy One found no place or spot to rest among us; yet He came to lay His head on the cross, that we might find a place for ourselves in the bosom of the Father.

28.5.5.en: When our inner tables are filled with filth, it is said to the Lord “there is no place” [8], instead of saying: “Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits” (Song 4:16).

28.5.6.en: Yet the Savior longs to prepare a place in Himself for us, saying to us: “Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon a rock: and it shall come to pass, while my glory passeth by, that I will put thee in a clift of the rock, and will cover thee with my hand while I pass by” (Ex 33:21-22).

28.6.0.en: D. Mockery of the prophet: The priests and false prophets in their drunkenness mocked the prophet Isaiah, saying: “Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts?” [9]. It is as though they were saying that they are people of knowledge and learning, so why does he want to teach them anything?! Let him go to those weaned from milk and present to them his prophecies and commandments, which are fitting only for the simple who have no thought and for infants who are not mature.

28.7.0.en: “For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little” [10]. It is as though the prophet were talking to small children, repeating to them commands and ordinances and offering them small things... It is like one who holds a child and teaches him to walk, pulling him now to the right and now to the left... a picture of the contempt of the drunken priests and prophets for the prophet Isaiah and his teachings!

28.8.0.en: What is the punishment of those who mock him and his teachings and prophecies? The prophet says: “For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people” [11]. They mocked the language of the prophet or his prophecies, supposing him to be one who teaches newly weaned children; therefore God sends them an enemy of strange tongue who cries out in their faces, and they do not understand his words, so they become like children without knowledge. They refused to learn from Isaiah and mocked him, so the Lord sent them Assyrian masters to teach them through the language of violence and enslavement together with humiliation.

28.9.0.en: “To whom he said, This is the rest (my rest) wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear” [12]. They did not wish to listen to the voice of God, who says that His rest is in our giving rest to the weary who are burdened with toils. The priests and false prophets cared for outward formalities, not for the rest of God Himself, who rests in His people.

28.9.1.en: * It was said by the prophet: “This is my rest: cause the weary to rest” [12]. Accomplish this rest for the Lord, O man, and then you will not need to say: “Forgive me.” Give rest to the weary, visit the sick, give food to the poor, for this in truth is prayer... All the time in which you fulfill the rest of the Lord is a time of prayer...

28.9.2.en: Beware, beloved, lest an opportunity come to you to give rest to the will of God and you say: Now is the time for prayer, I will pray and then I will work!

28.10.0.en: Father Aphrahat Let them listen to the voice of the Lord and speak with Him not in the language of formalities but in the language of practical obedience, comforting to God in His children. Let them learn this as children, and let them train in it, ignoring that they are priests and prophets who possess knowledge and learning, lest they fall backward and sink into the snares of the enemy like game or prey [13] whose end is certain death.

28.11.0.en: He answers these scoffers, saying: “We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves” [15]. They declare that they do not fear death or dread the grave, for they have entered into a covenant with them; they know how to take refuge in lies so that they do not fall under disciplines or afflictions, because their constitution is deceit.

28.11.1.en: They are a type of the Antichrist and his followers, as he is the tyrant who makes a covenant with the formalists in worship (Dan 9:27) so that they may act without fear of death or the grave; but the work of the Lord Christ is to shatter this covenant in order to establish a covenant with the Father and an eternal reconciliation with His believers.

28.12.0.en: 16 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste. 17 Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding place. 18 And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it. 19 From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you: for morning by morning shall it pass over, by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report. 20 For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it. 21 For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act. 22 Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong: for I have heard from the Lord GOD of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth.

28.12.1.en: If the enemy of good works with all his energies to turn believers away from the truth, working in different forms in every age, especially in the days of the apostasy (the Antichrist), the Lord Himself comes forward to support His children and believers against this satanic work.

28.12.2.en: “Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste” [16].

28.12.3.en: Thus, in the midst of the dark picture, the prophet Isaiah prophesies of the Messiah as the cornerstone and the foundation stone on which the Church is built:

28.12.4.en: A. The foundation stone in Zion: The psalmist says: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the LORD'S doing; it is marvellous in our eyes” (Ps 118:22-23) (see Mt 21:42; Acts 4:11; Rom 9:33; Eph 2:20; 1 Pet 2:6, 8); He is the foundation stone on which the Church is built, a tried stone, tested by Satan so that by His victory He might give us the victory; a precious stone beyond price. He is the cornerstone who joined the Jews with the Gentiles like two walls knit together in faith in Him. Whoever believes in Him will not flee (be put to shame)... Thus Isaiah gives us a Messianic prophecy that reveals the person of the Lord Christ and His place in relation to the Church, His riches and glory, and trust in Him, and His unchangeableness and rejection.

28.12.5.en: * The Savior is the chosen stone, rejected by those who should have built the synagogue of the Jews, and He has become the head of the corner. Scripture likens Him to a cornerstone because He joins the two peoples together: Israel and the Gentiles, in one faith and one love (Eph 2:15).

28.12.6.en: St. Cyril the Great * Who is this of whom we speak?

28.12.7.en: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner” (Ps 118:23); “to make in himself of twain one new man, so making peace; and that he might reconcile both unto God in one body” (Eph 2:15-16); that is, the circumcision and the uncircumcision.

28.13.0.en: St. Augustine B. A spiritual building is raised upon Him [17], whose measuring line is truth and whose plummet is justice. So the building is raised straight, with no crookedness, dwelt in by truth and justice, for God Himself dwells in it with His believers.

28.14.0.en: If the Church is the living building raised upon the person of the Lord Christ as her foundation, then His Gospel is the truth and His cross is the justice joined to mercy. By the Gospel and the cross the Church of Christ is built in uprightness as a place of safety. But whoever takes refuge in lies, like the false prophets, the hail becomes a refuge for them and the floods sweep away their hidden depths, so all their hope goes in vain and they lose safety. Their covenant with death and the grave is annulled, and the scourge sweeps them away like a flood that brings them down to the ground, so that they are trodden down [18]. With every morning and every evening, new disturbing news reaches them because of the continual attack of the enemies. They find no room enough to stretch out in sleep, nor a covering to wrap themselves in against the cold.

28.15.0.en: “For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon, that he may do his work, his strange work; and bring to pass his act, his strange act” [21].

28.15.1.en: “Perazim” is a Canaanite name meaning “breakings forth,” a place in the valley of Rephaim (2 Sam 5:20; 1 Chr 14:11); it is Mount Perazim near the valley of Gibeon and perhaps its site today is “Ras al-Sanadir.” Isaiah's saying here: “For the LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim” means that God storms upon His enemies suddenly and shatters them completely, just as He did for the prophet David at Mount Perazim when he said: “The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters” (2 Sam 5:20); and also his saying: “as in the valley of Gibeon” means that He works as in the days of Joshua against the Canaanites in the valley of Gibeon (Josh 10:10).

28.15.2.en: What is the strange work that God does but the punishing of wrong? For God takes no pleasure in punishing; He does so out of necessity, as a thing strange to Him, for Jeremiah says: “But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies. For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men” (Lam 3:32-33), as it is said: “For, behold, the LORD cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity” (Isa 26:21).

28.16.0.en: Thus the wicked, especially those who mock the word of the Lord and the prophecies and who refuse to believe in the Messiah, the subject of the prophecies and the center of all Scripture, find no mercy or refuge, in spite of God's unwillingness to punish. He says: “Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong” [22], meaning not the bands with which the people are bound when taken captive to Assyria or Babylon, but the chains of eternal darkness that bind those who deny the faith and reject the prophecies, when the whole earth is judged [22].

28.17.0.en: 23 Give ye ear, and hear my voice; hearken, and hear my speech. 24 Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground? 25 When he hath made plain the face thereof, doth he not cast abroad the fitches, and scatter the cummin, and cast in the principal wheat and the appointed barley and the rie in their place? 26 For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him. 27 For the fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod. 28 Bread corn is bruised; because he will not ever be threshing it, nor break it with the wheel of his cart, nor bruise it with his horsemen. 29 This also cometh forth from the LORD of hosts, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working.

28.17.1.en: He likens God to a sower who does not stop at plowing and breaking up the ground and preparing it for planting but also scatters the seed. If God permits discipline, it is like the sower who plows the ground and breaks it up and clears it of stones and levels it, and this is the negative work; but He does not stop there but offers a positive work, for He casts the seed of His word into the field of this world. The Lord Himself comes forward as a seed that He Himself casts into our hearts in order to establish His garden in us. He knows how to sow the fitches, Nigella Sativa [a plant of the buttercup family, with umbel-like flowers similar to the anise plant, whose seed is called the seed of blessing, and which is not threshed but beaten with a rod], and the cummin and the wheat and the barley and the rie, each in its place and in the way that suits it.

28.18.0.en: We are God's husbandry and His field and His vineyard; He cares for us as our own God, who belongs to us as we belong to Him, “For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him” [26]...

28.19.0.en: Like a sower who knows how to deal with each crop: some need threshing with the threshing instrument, and some need to be beaten with the rod to extract the seed from the chaff, and some need neither threshing nor beating [27]; and in all this He does not seek to destroy His crops and crush them but to gather them [28]... He is the compassionate God even in His disciplines, seeking what is for the salvation and edification of His children, working with wonderful wisdom and great understanding [29].
